note:
The manifest of every external input to this tree, code and data alike. Nothing enters the tree undeclared (plan L0 step 3). Entries are pinned by URL and SHA-256, never by version range, because rule R11 applies to code for the same reason it applies to data: upstream is mutable and a resolver hides that. See MANIFEST.md for the format.

ARCHIVES DECLARE WHAT IS TAKEN OUT OF THEM. An archive's SHA-256 pins the container and says nothing about which of its members this tree reads. Every entry with `unpack` therefore carries `consumes` — `whole-tree` where the archive is compiled entire, `declared-members` where it is not — and a `members` list giving each individually-read member its own SHA-256: the licence text quoted verbatim into NOTICE, the file compared against a populated FetchContent tree, or a data member extracted into the cache because something outside Python needs a path to it. tools/fetch.py refuses an archive entry that declares neither. The rule was prompted by EGM2008, which ships seven members of which this tree reads two and deliberately does not open hsynth_WGS84.f, and it applies to every archive rather than to the one that revealed it.

At 1 microsecond of TDB-TT error, ten times any error credibly attributed to the analytic series, the Sun's geocentric position moves 30 mm and the third-body acceleration by about 3.5e-15 m/s^2, which nothing in this tree can see. entries.role: Fehlberg, NASA TR R-287 (1968) — RK7(8) and RK8(9) coefficients (Tables X, XII), the truncation-error term (134), and Example (53) with its closed-form exact solution and published accumulated errors (Tables XI, XIII). SPEC-integrators, L3 step 2.
entries.version: NASA TR R-287, October 1968, 97 pages
entries.licence_note: NASA technical report, public domain.
entries.verify_note: THIS IS A 1968 SCAN AND ITS OCR IS UNUSABLE FOR THE MATHEMATICS. pdftotext renders Table X's beta block as '83_ = 841 = B_I = 8sl = B71 = Be1', and mangles even the contents page ('TABLE IN.' for III, 'SectionXVHI' for XVIII, '8O' for 80) -- the I/1 and O/0 confusions that matter most for digits. THE PAGE IMAGES ARE PERFECTLY LEGIBLE: rendered at 150 dpi, Table X (report p.65, PDF p.72) gives the coefficients as EXACT RATIONALS -- alpha = 0, 2/27, 1/9, 1/6, 5/12, 1/2, 5/6, 1/6, 2/3, 1/3, 1, 0, 1; c = 41/840, 34/105, 9/35, 9/280; TE = (41/840)(f0 + f10 - f11 - f12)h at (134). So the coefficients must be read from the IMAGES, not the text layer -- and, crucially, the transcription is then verified against the RUNGE-KUTTA ORDER CONDITIONS, which are exact algebraic identities independent of the scan. A misread digit fails them. The source's legibility is therefore not what the gate rests on.
